newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela quake victims call help on cellphones.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela quake victims call help on cellphones.

text.p: Rescuers redoubled efforts on Thursday to dig out trapped survivors of Venezuela's worst earthquake in three decades who called for help on mobile telephones from under a collapsed building.
Franciso Espin, Civil Defence director for Sucre state, said rescue workers were trying to pass oxygen lines to people buried under the six-floor building in the state capital Cumana.

As 300 firemen and medics swarmed over the rubble, one of the buried callers, lawyer Carlos Navarro, said he was trapped with seven others still alive after the Seguros La Seguridad office block crashed to the ground on Wednesday afternoon.
Authorities said nine survivors had so been freed from the building -- the main focus of rescue attempts -- and 10 bodies recovered.
The earthquake, which measured 6.9 on the Richter scale, rocked Venezuela's eastern Caribbean coast at about 3.25 p.m. EDT (1725 GMT) on Wednesday, killing at least 59 people.
Venezuela is the most developed cellular phone market in the region, analysts say, with subscription rates comparable to those in the United States.
